text:
Marathon Petroleum is up 1.66% today, continuing a sharp two-week rally of 22.6%. The stock has climbed as oil prices have spiked amid escalating Middle East tensions—container ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities have raised concerns about supply disruptions, pushing crude prices higher and widening the profit margins refineries earn by turning cheap oil into expensive fuel. US oil is trading at $96.24 a barrel, up sharply from earlier in the period, and refineries are running at 92.7% utilization, keeping throughput high.

The broader backdrop is a refiner's near-ideal environment: crude prices have jumped more than $20 a barrel globally (world oil at $125.44), geopolitical risk is supporting those prices, and the company is running at near-full capacity with strong demand. The stock's momentum over the past week suggests investors are pricing in sustained high refining margins as long as Middle East tensions—and therefore the oil price premium—persist.
